answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil identities by requiring each account to lock a ferrous bond before bidding for scarce tasks. Rewards arrive only after verified work, so fake accounts add no output: each must fund a separate stake and bear its opportunity cost. A randomly selected summit of reviewers checks disputed claims and can slash the bond. An attacker must pay capital for every identity and risks losing each stake if caught; honest agents recover their bond after completing work. An anchor rule can also cap one account's share of tasks, limiting the gains from creating identities.
